events.credibility_reason: Two versions withdrawn without notice; a reported earlier title claiming a proof could not be confirmed.
The restricted classes and the equivalence of the restated conjecture come only from search summaries; the body was not read.

Five years with no uptake on a landmark claim; Mikhailov's 2026 papers call the question open and do not cite it; the author's earlier preprint on the question has withdrawn versions; an unverified quote has the paper conceding no progress at one step.

No uptake after 3.5 years on a landmark claim; later specialist papers call the question open and do not cite it; flagged gaps (a Euclidean-type reduction whose termination for infinite bases is unclear, inconsistent definitions in Lemma 5.1, a key lemma from an unrefereed preprint); the journal publication could not be verified.

events.ai_basis: A variety of AI tools, including ChatGPT 6 Astra, Claude 5.5 Fable, and Aristotle, were used to assist with the proof of the main results and the redaction of the manuscript.
The vast majority of results were obtained with the same procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model.

why: Only two events claim the whole statement, Pasku (July 2021) and Kawauchi (March 2023). Both first appeared before the snapshot, and the record shows no new mathematics in their later revisions (Oct 2026 and Apr 2024), so both are dated before it. Both are unreviewed and doubtful: nobody has taken them up, and the 2026 specialist papers call the question open without citing either. They are not knocked down, because no specific unanswered error is on the record. After the snapshot, nothing settles a case or moves the statement. Harlander-Rosebrock 2025 concerns local indicability; DR subcomplexes of DR complexes are DR trivially, and injective LOTs were already known to be aspherical, so it adds no case of asphericity. Mikhailov's finite chain answers Hitchman's question. Bartholdi-Mikhailov produce finite chains that the authors themselves say do not give the infinite chain a counterexample needs, so the scope is none. Their AI statement says the tools assisted 'with the proof of the main results', so that event is marked assisted. The OpenAI release is about Eilenberg-Ganea, a different conjecture; by Bestvina-Brady its failure does not decide Whitehead, so it is a variant. Its AI role is taken from the README's statement about the release as a whole.
doubts: Whether Pasku 2021 should be not_credible rather than doubtful is a close call. Several F10 signals are present, but the author works in the area with a serious method. The choice cannot change the outcome, because the event predates the snapshot and is unreviewed. The OpenAI AI credit rests on a release-wide README sentence, not on a statement specific to this paper. The Bartholdi-Mikhailov quote does not say which steps the AI contributed.
